new_statements.quote: All of the forms may be assumed to have penultimate stress on the root unless otherwise marked although with some sources it is hard to determine the facts about stress (if stress is relevant at all) and so stress may not be consistently represented. [p.3] ... While [zaq] is extremely similar to [zae], [zaq] tends to drop the post-tonic vowel in normal speech. [fn.145, p.40]
new_statements.citation: Marlett, Stephen A. (compiler). 2010 [February 2010 revision]. Basic vocabulary. In Cheryl A. Black, H. Andrew Black & Stephen A. Marlett (eds.), The Zapotec grammar files. SIL International (SIL-Mexico electronic working papers WP001). 66 pp. [with companion files: Marlett 2009 'Transcription conventions' (5 pp.) and Marlett 2010 'Data sources' (11 pp.)]
new_statements.locator: Introduction p.3 (stress convention); footnote 145 p.40 (zaq post-tonic vowel); zaq forms with explicit non-default stress marks e.g. bisˈte (1.213, p.3), ijːaˈba (p.12), biˈju (p.21), leˈbiˀ (p.24), lazˈdo ~ lazˈto (p.37), ɾiˈsa/iˈsa/biˈsa (p.51), ʐiˈna (p.58)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: statement check: group-level-statement. The quoted sentence is the compiler's transcription default for every Zapotec variety in the file ('may be assumed.. if stress is relevant at all'), not an analysis of Aloapam; the only zaq-specific remark (fn. 145, post-tonic vowel drop, verified in the mirror extract) implies stress exists but not where it falls. Usable only as 'root-penult by convention, several zaq items marked root-final'. | checker: copies we hold re-extracted with extracted text (67 pp.). Introduction, printed p.3: 'All of the forms may be assumed to have penultimate stress on the root unless otherwise marked although with some sources it is hard to determine the facts about st…
new_statements.relation_note: Stress default (root-penultimate) + explicit stress marks on zaq forms + zaq post-tonic vowel loss; fn. 'the lenis stop /d/ is voiceless in [zaq]'; Transcription conventions sec. 3.5: tone diacritics only 'if included' — none included for zaq.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Compiler's default for all varieties in the file, Aloápam included: stress on the penultimate syllable of the ROOT (prefixes do not count) unless a form is marked otherwise; the Aloápam column marks root-final stress explicitly on a handful of items (bisˈte, biˈju, lazˈdo, ʐiˈna, ɾiˈsa..), and a zaq-specific note says Aloápam drops the post-tonic vowel in normal speech (so word stress is phonetically real in zaq). No tone is transcribed for the zaq forms.
new_statements.exceptions: Forms 'otherwise marked' (several zaq items carry ˈ before the final syllable); hedge that for some sources 'it is hard to determine the facts about stress (if stress is relevant at all)'.
new_statements.identity_note: Row 'zaq Aloápam' in every table (ISO code + Ethnologue name; Data sources gives INALI name 'zapoteco de San Miguel Aloápam'); 23 tables, c. 70 zaq cells in broad IPA. Contributor for zaq not named in the Jan-2010 Data sources (cell empty); fn.145 compares zaq with Yareni [zae], Thiessen's variety. Not listed in ITEM.our_bibliography (it was downloaded by the 2026-09-19 lexical pass and sits in the held dir).

sources.citation: SIL International language page for zaq (www.sil.org/resources/search/language/zaq), Internet Archive copy 2015-09-07: full list of 18 SIL archive items for Aloápam Zapotec
sources.note: Inventory only: readers, riddles, number book, alphabet charts, vowel colouring book, the 2-page Ortografía (2001), two picture dictionaries. No grammar, phonology sketch or dictionary with grammar notes exists in the SIL archive list for zaq.

sources.citation: Nellis, Neil & Jane Goodner Nellis (comps.). 1983. Diccionario zapoteco de Juárez (Atepec, Ixtlán), with Bartholomew, Doris, 'Gramática zapoteca'. Vocabularios Indígenas 27. México: ILV.
sources.note: Nearest fully described sister variety (Sierra de Juárez Zapotec, zaa) with explicit tone/stress description; useful as a proxy or for the identity note, but it is a different glottocode (sier1250-area), not Aloápam.

sources.citation: Radin, Paul. 1925. The distribution and phonetics of the Zapotec dialects: a preliminary sketch. Journal de la Société des Américanistes 17: 27-76. [Glottolog ref 103699]
sources.note: Lists 'Aloapa' among the Serrano pueblos ('All the puebloes in this group form a fixed unit with the exception of Abejones, Aloapa and Xia', p.30) and says of Zapotec generally 'The vowels are characterized by the possession of pitch accent' (p.31) and mentions 'loss of old pitch accent' (p.34); no statement on where word stress falls in any variety, and no Aloápam-specific phonetic remarks.
sources.venue: Journal de la Société des Américanistes 17

sources.citation: Ca Tisa gue Tata Jesucristuha: El Nuevo Testamento, zapoteco de Aloápam. 1a ed. 2020, Wycliffe Bible Translators; versión electrónica 2022 (scriptureearth.org). 724 pp.
sources.note: No alphabet or pronunciation preface/appendix (checked front matter, back matter and a full-text search for stress/accent acento/alfabeto/pronuncia). The practical orthography marks an acute accent on some vowels (sitá, bilátia, Gualíba, esíaya, carbáru), implying accent is written where not default, but no rule is stated.

sources.citation: SIL International, Mexico Branch (Aloápam Zapotec programme; narrators incl. Clemente Cruz Cruz). 2007/2022. Bartholomew Collection of Unpublished Materials, SIL Language & Culture Archives. 477 pp. CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
sources.note: No phonology content: archive notice + raw interlinear texts only. The practical orthography writes acute accents on some vowels (biyú, nasá, sitá) and underlines others (gue̱, ree̱), i.e. prosodic MARKS without any statement of what they encode (wordlist/text-level data only, not a statement).
